recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. The current source satisfies the Published Jira request; no follow-up is needed unless FHIR-I later reopens chained _has behavior.
issue_request: FHIR-20474 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Search clarification asking to document that _has, as a valid search parameter for all resources, can be used inside a chained search path. The requested example was GET [base]/Encounter?patient._has:Group:member:_id=102.
initial_application: Commit f01805bc3874656f880d48d77a4b4c91dafaf3e9, titled "FHIR-20474 - Example of chaining and reverse chaining", added the Encounter patient._has Group membership example to source/search.html on 2022-08-26. Current blame still traces the substantive example and explanatory sentence to that commit.
additional_context: The linked Zulip thread confirms the motivating question and agreement that the behavior should be documented. Jira searches found other reverse-chaining issues, but no later final decision that removes or contradicts this example. Confluence has no indexed references to FHIR-20474.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source/search.html section on reverse chaining includes both GET and POST forms of the requested chained _has example and explains that it searches for Encounters of patients who are members of Group "102".

related_jiras.note: Older Published issue about removing restrictions from _has, relevant only as general reverse-chaining history.
Separate Published issue about advertising reverse-chaining support in CapabilityStatement/SearchParameter, not the chained _has example.
